- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.80 or 80.24), often overshooting by 2–5 points.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), failing to capture mean reversion toward historical levels.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the forecast window.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, underreacting to sudden drops or spikes in the history.
- For horizon > 15 days, model exhibits a systematic underestimation of the true mean price, especially when history shows strong upward momentum.
- Model often fails to adjust for recent price corrections — it retains old momentum patterns even after sharp declines.
